Equations in Word, PowerPoint and HTML

Source: vignettes/articles/word-powerpoint-html.Rmd
word-powerpoint-html.Rmd
library(equatags)

transform_mathjax() converts equations written in LaTeX into the formats of documents:

  • to = "mml": ‘Office Open XML Math’, the native format of equations in Word and PowerPoint. The equations stay editable in Word or PowerPoint.
  • to = "html": the HTML of ‘KaTeX’, displayed with the CSS of ‘KaTeX’.

The equations are read by ‘KaTeX’: the functions supported by KaTeX can be used (fractions, scripts, sums and integrals, roots, matrices and arrays, \left( \right), accents, arrows, \text{}, colours…). An equation that ‘KaTeX’ can not read is an error.

HTML 

x <- transform_mathjax("x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}", to = "html")
substr(x, 1, 120)
#> [1] "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" type=\"text/css\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.9/dist/katex.min.css\" data-external"

The result starts with a link to the CSS of ‘KaTeX’ and can be written as is in an HTML page or an R Markdown document (chunk option results = "asis"):

cat(x)

x=−b±b2−4ac2ax = x=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

Inline and display style

Equations are inline by default, as $...$ in LaTeX. With display = TRUE, they use the display style, as $$...$$: larger fractions, limits of sums above and below the operator.

cat(transform_mathjax("\\sum_{i=1}^{n} \\frac{x_i}{n}", to = "html"))

∑i=1nxin_{i=1}^{n} ∑i=1n​nxi​​

cat(transform_mathjax("\\sum_{i=1}^{n} \\frac{x_i}{n}", to = "html", display = TRUE))

∑i=1nxin_{i=1}^{n} i=1∑n​nxi​​

Word

With to = "mml", each equation is an <m:oMath> element:

eq <- transform_mathjax("x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}", to = "mml", display = TRUE)
cat(substr(eq, 1, 300))
#> 
#> <m:oMath xmlns:m="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/math">
#>   <m:r>
#>     <m:t>x=</m:t>
#>   </m:r>
#>   <m:f>
#>     <m:fPr>
#>       <m:type m:val="bar"/>
#>     </m:fPr>
#>     <m:num>
#>       <m:r>
#>         <m:t>−b±</m:t>
#>       </m:r>
#>       <m:rad>
#>         <m:radPr>
#>           <m:degHide m:val="on"/

It can be inserted in a Word document with ‘officer’, in a paragraph (w:p) written with officer::body_add_xml(). An equation alone in its paragraph is written in a math paragraph (m:oMathPara), as Word does; an equation in a sentence is written next to the runs of text:

library(officer)

ns_w <- "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
ns_m <- "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/math"

# an equation alone in its paragraph
alone <- sprintf(
  '<w:p xmlns:w="%s"><m:oMathPara xmlns:m="%s">%s</m:oMathPara></w:p>',
  ns_w, ns_m, eq
)
# an equation in a sentence
euler <- transform_mathjax("e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0", to = "mml")
sentence <- sprintf(
  '<w:p xmlns:w="%s"><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Euler: </w:t></w:r>%s</w:p>',
  ns_w, euler
)

doc <- read_docx()
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "The quadratic formula:")
doc <- body_add_xml(doc, str = alone)
doc <- body_add_xml(doc, str = sentence)
print(doc, target = tempfile(fileext = ".docx"))

Equations get the default font size of the document and the math font of the document (‘Cambria Math’ unless another one is chosen in Word). The argument rpr gives them run properties, for example a size of 16 points (w:sz is in half points) and a colour:

eq <- transform_mathjax(
  "a^2 + b^2 = c^2",
  to = "mml",
  rpr = '<w:rPr><w:sz w:val="32"/><w:color w:val="C0392B"/></w:rPr>'
)

rpr has one value for all equations or one value per equation.

PowerPoint

In PowerPoint, the same equations are given run properties of PowerPoint (<a:rPr>, size in hundredths of a point) and are embedded in a text box. The simplest way is ‘flextable’, which writes the equations of its cells in Word, PowerPoint and HTML, with the size and the colour of the cell:

library(flextable)

dat <- data.frame(
  name = c("Quadratic formula", "Normal density"),
  formula = c(
    "x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}",
    "f(x) = \\frac{1}{\\sigma\\sqrt{2\\pi}} e^{-\\frac{(x-\\mu)^2}{2\\sigma^2}}"
  )
)
ft <- flextable(dat)
ft <- mk_par(ft, j = "formula", value = as_paragraph(as_equation(formula)))
ft <- autofit(ft)
ft

name

formula

Quadratic formula

x=−b±b2−4ac2ax = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}x=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

Normal density

f(x)=1σ2πe−(x−μ)22σ2f(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}f(x)=σ2π​1​e−2σ2(x−μ)2​

The same table goes to a Word document with save_as_docx() and to a PowerPoint presentation with save_as_pptx(). autofit() uses the size of the equations computed by equation_size() (see the article “Size and drawing of equations”).

Accented characters

‘KaTeX’ warns about characters it does not know in math mode, such as accented letters. With strict = "ignore" (the default), they are accepted silently; strict = "warn" and strict = "error" report them.
